SourcesBox score, game stories and the drawn play

Box score from the Minnesota Timberwolves' 106–98 home win over the Portland Trail Blazers at Target Center on Nov 16, 2026, from the Covers box score, with game details from the Associated Press (via CBS Minnesota and KAAL), Field Level Media (via The Ticket), TSN, Timberwolves On SI and Blazers On SI. All 106 Minnesota points and all 98 Portland points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: 26–26 after one, 59–51 Minnesota at the half, 87–73 after three. Team stats (free throws 30 of 39 to 12 of 15, rebounds 53–49, steals 7–5, fast-break points 18–7, points in the paint 44–46, threes 10 of 34 to 12 of 41, biggest leads 20 and 10) are from the same box score. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Monday's games.

Portland led by as many as 10 in the first quarter before a 12–2 Minnesota run tied it 24–24 (Field Level Media). Minnesota scored the last six points of the half, McDaniels's layup at 1:35, Kuminga's reverse dunk at 1:11 and Shannon's driving layup with 53.7 seconds left, to lead 59–51 at the break (Field Level Media; AP). Shannon's 3-pointer and two free throws late in the third made it 87–70, and Minnesota led by 14 going into the fourth; Portland closed on an 11–1 run after both teams emptied their benches (Field Level Media; AP). Shannon's 34 points were a career high, 12 of them in the second quarter (AP), and tied the most by a Wolves reserve in 10 years (TSN). Minnesota has won six of seven and is 7–3 with Anthony Edwards out after knee surgery (AP; TSN). Jaylen Clark missed the game with a right hamstring strain (AP). The teams meet again Tue, Nov 17 at 8:00 PM ET in Minneapolis.

The play of the game is an original illustration of Terrence Shannon Jr.'s driving layup with 53.7 seconds left in the second quarter that made it 59–51 (Field Level Media; the AP and the Covers line score confirm 59–51 at the half). Timberwolves On SI describes his early push of the pace as drives and transition layups; the recaps don't describe this drive further, so it is drawn as a plain drive to a short finish. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Shannon's listed 6-foot-6 and 215 pounds (Basketball-Reference; Wikipedia), with arms scaled to his reported 6-foot-8 wingspan (Sportskeeda), in Minnesota's home white. Sources disagree on his current number (No. 1 or No. 00), so no number is drawn. He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn in the kit with our default skin tone. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
